item.title: China's trade promotion body sends over 6,000 delegations abroad in three years to tap global markets
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
China's trade promotion body sends over 6,000 delegations abroad in three years to tap global markets Attendees listen closely to a speaker at the Global Trade and Investment Promotion Summit 2026 in Beijing, capital of China. (Xinhua/Li Xin) Over the past three years, China's national trade promotion system has organized more than 6,000 business delegations to visit other countries, as part of an initiative to send business delegations abroad to help Chinese companies find partners and markets. In August, more than 100 Chinese entrepreneurs traveled to Kyrgyzstan as part of the largest Chinese business delegation to visit the country in recent years. In July, a delegation of Chinese entrepreneurs visited Salt Lake City, Chicago and Washington to explore new areas of economic cooperation with the U.S. Earlier trips this year took Chinese business delegations to countries including the UK, Morocco, Türkiye, Kenya, South Africa, Turkmenistan, Belarus and Mozambique. In the first eight months of this year, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) sent 173 delegations to 43 countries and regions. Finding opportunities "Local development needs are becoming more specific, and the room for us to get involved is getting clearer," said Wen Peng, chairman of Henan SRON Silo Engineering Co., Ltd. (SRON), describing his biggest takeaway from his trip to Kyrgyzstan this August. This was his third visit to Kyrgyzstan as a member of a CCPIT business delegation. SRON specializes in bulk storage and logistics solutions for grain, building materials, minerals and coal. He said Kyrgyzstan's relatively high post-harvest grain losses point to real opportunities in agricultural infrastructure and storage. A Chinese business delegation, organized by the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, meets with the U.S.-China Business Council and its member companies in Washington on July 31. (Xinhua/Li Rui) "This lines up closely with our business, so we didn't treat the trip as just another business visit. It was when we really started paying attention to Kyrgyzstan and the broader Central Asian market and thinking about what we could actually offer there," Wen said. This also marked Wen's eighth time joining a CCPIT-organized business delegation, with previous trips taking him to Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Russia, Austria and Italy, among other countries. "For us, this kind of on-the-ground research is both a breakthrough journey into markets like Central Asia and a learning journey that builds our capacity to operate internationally," he said, adding that in-person visits are essential for understanding local industry, market conditions and development plans. China's foreign trade in goods totaled 30.13 trillion yuan (about $4.49 trillion) in the first seven months of the year, up 17.3 percent year on year, maintaining its position as the world's largest trader in goods. "Behind this growth are foreign trade companies working hard to seize opportunities, and CCPIT has consistently supported them in practical ways," said CCPIT spokesperson Yang Fan. Gaining confidence Luo Feng, senior expert and general manager of the overseas division at Hunan Bosen Industrial Group Co., Ltd., joined a CCPIT delegation for the first time this year and came away encouraged by Kyrgyzstan's enthusiasm for cooperation with Chinese companies — from infrastructure and industrial parks to agriculture and tourism. Bosen is now pursuing a digital trade infrastructure project in Kyrgyzstan that combines a computing center, manufacturing and overseas warehousing. Members of a Chinese business delegation tour Zhongda China Petrol Company during a visit to Kyrgyzstan on Aug. 29. (Photo/Xu Jingyi) China has remained Kyrgyzstan’s top trading partner and largest source of investment for years. Bilateral trade in goods reached a record $27.2 billion in 2025, up 20 percent year on year. Despite a complex and shifting global landscape, business communities around the world remain eager to pursue trade and economic exchange. Bosen, which has built projects across the Middle East, North America and Australia and served more than 4,000 companies, sees rising demand for cooperation as global supply chains become more integrated. Meanwhile, China's expanding market and culture of innovation continue to exert a powerful pull. The U.S.-China Business Council’s latest report found that 92 percent of surveyed U.S. companies had profitable China operations in 2025, while 95 percent said those operations helped boost their global competitiveness. Turning visits into projects After the Kyrgyzstan trip, Wang Zhigao, director of the park service center at Yangling Modern Agriculture International Cooperation Group Co., Ltd., stayed behind to check on a China-Kyrgyzstan apple demonstration orchard at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's agricultural base. This marked his fifth visit to the country. The demonstration orchard has introduced eight advanced apple varieties and 7,200 saplings using dwarfing, high-density planting and smart irrigation technologies, and has already produced its first harvest, Wang said. At a trade cooperation roundtable held during the visit, Wang shared his experience with Kyrgyz representatives, drawing interest from many companies eager to discuss potential partnerships. The trip to Kyrgyzstan brought together more than 100 representatives from Chinese companies spanning a wide range of industries, under a CCPIT-organized delegation. During the trip, business representatives from both countries signed more than 10 cooperation agreements or letters of intent, covering agriculture, energy, engineering equipment, construction materials and the digital economy. Yangling Modern Agriculture International Cooperation Group Co., Ltd. has built 14 overseas agricultural parks in countries including Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tanzania. By the end of July, CCPIT had approved 976 overseas exhibition projects for 2026 in Belt and Road partner countries, covering 48 countries, with 347 already carried out and nearly 9,000 companies participating. China's national trade promotion system issued 3,389,300 certificates of origin worth $212.34 billion to Belt and Road partner countries and nearly 4,924 ATA Carnets covering goods worth 1.34 billion yuan. "China's market will create even more growth opportunities, Chinese manufacturing will build a more efficient industrial ecosystem, and Chinese innovation will generate new business forms, scenarios and models," said CCPIT chairman Ren Hongbin, adding that the country will continue pursuing high-quality development and greater openness. item.title: Shenzhen streamlines customs clearance to facilitate smoother trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Shenzhen streamlines customs clearance to facilitate smoother trade Photo shows a busy scene at Yantian Port in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. (Photo/Zhu Haipeng) Walking into the operations and control center of Shenzhen Customs, one can see on a large screen the bustling movement of vehicles and vessels at ports across the city. Meanwhile, the day's customs clearance overview shows, through individual customs declarations, the trade ties and industrial cooperation between Shenzhen, Guangdong province, and other Asia-Pacific economies. At 11 a.m., at Shenzhen Bay Port, customs officers completed final inspections and cleared an export shipment of 144 mini personal computers. The goods were headed overseas via Hong Kong International Airport. Manufactured by CTOne Group, these compact smart computing terminals are no larger than a dictionary yet pack high-performance computing power. Capable of supporting local deployment of large AI models, they are designed for a broad range of applications -- from industrial control and smart offices to home entertainment and edge computing, making them popular in overseas markets. "We used to compete on price; now we compete on computing power and user experience," said Dai Yuanjun, president of the company. As artificial intelligence (AI) applications continue to develop rapidly worldwide, other Asia-Pacific economies are seeing strong demand for high-performance, portable smart terminals. The company's proprietary brands, including CYX and ACEMAGIC, are gradually gaining recognition. The company recently established a production base in Mexico, becoming part of the Asia-Pacific AI industry and supply chain, and now holds nearly 20 percent of the global mini PC market. An engineer tests products at Shenzhen CYX Industrial Co., Ltd. in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. (Photo/ilonghua.sznews.com) Many components used in these mini PCs are sourced from other Asia-Pacific economies. As a hub for processing trade, Shenzhen's manufacturing sector draws on highly responsive supply chains to export processed products across the region, promoting deeper integration of industrial chains. That afternoon, at DaChan Bay Terminal in Shenzhen, an ocean-going vessel loaded with lithium battery energy storage cabinets made by Chinese automaker BYD departed for Chile. The new equipment will support local photovoltaic power projects, contributing to the country's green energy transition. "Overseas orders for energy storage products are growing strongly, and exports are increasingly shifting toward long-term supply agreements," said Liu Feng, manager of customs affairs at BYD. Chinese-made energy storage cabinets are seeing a surge in orders in overseas wind and photovoltaic power markets thanks to their strong cost-performance ratio and high reliability, Liu said. "We have made comprehensive use of trade facilitation measures, including advance declarations, direct loading upon arrival at the port and 24/7 appointment-based inspections, significantly shortening customs clearance times," said Yang Nan, a first-level administrative law enforcement officer with the terminal supervision section of DaChan Bay Customs, under Shenzhen Customs. From January to July this year, DaChan Bay Customs handled 1,674 export shipments of the so-called "new trio" products, worth 5.385 billion yuan (about $803 million), up 31.71 percent and 33.82 percent year on year, respectively. The "New trio" refers to electric vehicles, lithium batteries, and solar products. Shenzhen Customs officers conduct an on-site inspection of imported Thai Monthong durians. (Photo courtesy of Shenzhen Customs) According to Shenzhen Customs, the city's exports to other Asia-Pacific economies are shifting rapidly toward emerging, high-value products. In the first half of this year, "new trio" products, AI-enabled products, medical instruments and equipment, and other such products accounted for 29.5 percent of Shenzhen's exports to other Asia-Pacific economies. At 6 p.m., at Shekou container terminal in Shenzhen, temperature-controlled containers carrying 36 tonnes of fresh apples from New Zealand were unloaded. This order from across the ocean was handled by Shenzhen Yuanxing Fruit Co., Ltd. "Since mid-August, we have seen an increasingly diverse range of imported fruits, including dragon fruit from Vietnam, and fresh coconuts from Thailand," said Zheng Jingsen, an executive at the company. "Thanks to the tariff concessions and customs clearance facilitation brought by the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), high-quality fruits from across the Asia-Pacific are entering the Chinese market at a much faster pace," Zheng said. He added that the company has long cooperated with ASEAN member states, Australia, New Zealand and Chile. It has also established a fruit and vegetable processing base in Vietnam, connecting Asia-Pacific orchards with China's vast consumer market. As night falls and the city lights up, Shenzhen's customs clearance overview continues to update. Data from Shenzhen Customs show that the city's imports and exports with other APEC economies rose from 267.5 billion yuan in 1996 to 3.13 trillion yuan in 2025, an average annual growth rate of 8.5 percent and an increase of more than tenfold. Through trade, China and other Asia-Pacific economies are jointly writing a new chapter of shared opportunities and mutual benefit. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Hong Kong unveils maiden 5-year plan, charts roadmap for high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Hong Kong unveils maiden 5-year plan, charts roadmap for high-quality development HONG KONG, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) on Wednesday unveiled its first five-year plan for economic and social development (2026-2030), a milestone as it enters a new phase of becoming more prosperous. The plan will help build a more open, inclusive, liberal, prosperous and safer Hong Kong, said HKSAR Chief Executive John Lee. Unveiling the blueprint, Lee said the 2026-2030 period is five crucial years for Hong Kong to seize the opportunity to enhance social well-being and build a better home for all. Comprising seven parts and 28 chapters, the plan sets out a total of 105 indicators spanning a wide range of areas. Key objectives include achieving new breakthroughs in economic development, boosting international competitiveness and influence, as well as significantly improving public well-being. According to the plan, Hong Kong's real GDP growth rate is projected to remain within a reasonable range during the 2026-2030 period, while the value added of the tourism industry is expected to rise about 40 to 50 percent to 126 billion Hong Kong dollars (about 16.06 billion U.S. dollars) by 2030. Hong Kong aims to elevate the ratio of total domestic expenditure on innovation activities to GDP to 3 after 2030, compared with a reading of 1.63 in 2024, the plan said. To sharpen its competitive edge, Hong Kong plans to consolidate and enhance its status as an international financial, maritime and trade center, and develop itself into an international innovation and technology center and a global hub for high-caliber talent, according to the blueprint. Efforts will also be made to expedite the development of the Northern Metropolis, deepen the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and create an international collaboration network. Social well-being has been high on the HKSAR government's agenda. While prioritizing young people's education, employment, entrepreneurship and home ownership, the government also pledged to eliminate substandard subdivided units by 2030. According to the plan, Hong Kong will supply 196,000 public flats in the coming five years, aiming to cut the average waiting time to under four years by 2030-31. The document also underscored efforts to adopt a holistic approach to development and security, boost governance efficacy, and strengthen the institutional safeguards for implementation. Delivering the policy address for 2026 shortly after presenting the blueprint, Lee said key policy initiatives and projects in the policy address will serve as core drivers to implement the five-year plan through enhanced inter-departmental coordination and regular progress reviews. To better solicit public opinion on the city's future development, the HKSAR government held over 100 consultation sessions over the past three months, receiving over 17,000 submissions on the five-year plan and 11,000 on the policy address. Noting this year marks the beginning of China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), Lee said that the inaugural blueprint represented a major initiative by the HKSAR government to uphold and enhance the executive-led system and improve governance efficacy. The blueprint underscored the strategic need for Hong Kong to proactively align with national development strategies and better integrate into the overall national development, while also laying out an action agenda to promote Hong Kong's high-quality development, the chief executive said. item.title: China pushes BeiDou navigation system deeper into global markets
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
China pushes BeiDou navigation system deeper into global markets CHANGSHA, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- China is advancing its BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) deeper into global markets, unveiling new products, technologies and applications at a summit in central China this week, as it seeks to position the system as a shared global service. At the 5th International Summit on BDS Applications held in Zhuzhou, Hunan Province, an international cooperation and innovation base for BeiDou applications was formally inaugurated, with plans to build a series of flagship overseas application demonstration projects and gradually construct a cooperation framework linking China's BeiDou industry with international markets. China has been steadily advancing the overseas rollout of BeiDou technology, products, standards and services, integrating the system into global infrastructure and serving economic and social development in Belt and Road countries. A report on BeiDou industry development released at the summit said that since completing global networking in 2020, the system's global service capabilities have continued to strengthen, with the foundation in place to provide stable, reliable and continuous services worldwide. BeiDou's capabilities in positioning, navigation, timing and short-message communication have continued to improve, reinforcing its global expansion in high-precision applications such as transportation, agriculture, marine fisheries and emergency rescue, according to the report. BeiDou has been fully incorporated into the standards systems of 11 international organizations, including the International Civil Aviation Organization, the International Maritime Organization and COSPAS-SARSAT, an international satellite system for search and rescue, covering core areas like civil aviation, maritime affairs and mobile communications. Zhang Junping, a Hunan provincial government official overseeing business services, said BeiDou is now one of four global satellite navigation systems recognized by the United Nations, with related products exported to more than 140 countries and regions. In Belt and Road countries, BeiDou applications and products account for 58 percent of the market, he noted. Zhang cited projects ranging from smart port operations at Peru's Chancay port to BeiDou monitoring on the China-Maldives Friendship Bridge, and from precision agriculture in Laos to taxi dispatch in Cambodia. Experts at the summit said satellite navigation is not a zero-sum game, and that BeiDou is willing to be compatible and interoperable with other global navigation systems to jointly build global spatial-temporal infrastructure. Demonstration projects have already been implemented in multiple African and Southeast Asian countries for land surveying, disaster monitoring and fisheries management. Myo Thant, deputy director general of the Myanmar Space Agency, said there is considerable potential for BeiDou applications in Myanmar, particularly in high-precision positioning, transportation, agriculture, surveying and mapping, and disaster management. "Myanmar is keen to deepen practical cooperation with China and other stakeholders in technical standards, testing and certification, professional training, capacity building, technology transfer and the development of practical BeiDou application projects," Thant added. BeiDou now provides signal coverage to over 200 countries and regions. Its international promotion is entering a key transition period from broad expansion to deeper value creation, and from product exports to ecosystem building, the report said. item.title: China opens major river-to-sea canal, creating trade shortcut to Southeast Asia
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
China opens major river-to-sea canal, creating trade shortcut to Southeast Asia NANNING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- China opened the Pinglu Canal on Wednesday, giving its landlocked southwest a shortcut to the coast and overseas markets, particularly those in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), the country's largest trading partner. Built at a cost of 72.7 billion yuan (about 10.75 billion U.S. dollars), the 134.2-kilometer canal runs from Hengzhou, a county-level city in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, to the Beibu Gulf, the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China. The canal stretches along the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, a strategic trade route connecting China's inland regions with ASEAN and other global markets. It is the first river-to-sea canal project planned and coordinated at the national level since the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. A drone photo taken on Sept. 16, 2026 shows the Qinzhou Port area of Beibu Gulf Port in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Zhang Ailin) Designed for vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes, the canal shortens the inland waterway journey for goods from southwest China to the sea by more than 560 kilometers compared with traditional routes through ports in Guangdong Province. It is expected to reduce overall logistics costs by 18 to 30 percent and save more than 5 billion yuan in transportation costs each year. Lu Xinning, vice chairperson of the regional government of Guangxi, said the canal creates a new link between China's market of 1.4 billion people and ASEAN's nearly 700 million consumers. Its impact, Lu said, could extend beyond the movement of goods, spurring new cross-border investment and deepening regional supply-chain integration. The canal took over four years to build. Most of it was created by widening, deepening and straightening existing waterways, while a small section had to be excavated through dry land and mountainous terrain. This photo taken on Sept. 16, 2026 shows the Madao Hub on the Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing) "There was no established model or ready-made precedent to follow," said Cheng Yaofei, chairman of Guangxi Pinglu Canal Construction Co., Ltd. One of the biggest engineering challenges was a 65-meter difference in water level, roughly the height of a 20-plus-story building. Three navigation hubs, all featuring twin-line ship locks, were built to raise and lower vessels along the canal. Engineers developed water-recycling systems at the hubs, enabling the canal to save more than 1 billion cubic meters of water annually. Environmental protection was another priority during construction. More than 98 percent of the roughly 315 million cubic meters of earth and rock excavated during construction was reused. The canal also includes a fish passage more than 480 meters long and a dedicated wildlife crossing for land animals including leopard cats and squirrels. A drone photo taken on June 8, 2026 shows a view of the dedicated wildlife corridor bridge of the Pinglu Canal in Jiuzhou Town, Lingshan County of Qinzhou City in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Zhou Hua) The canal opens in the first year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), as the world's second-largest economy seeks to promote more coordinated regional development and further expand high-standard opening up -- priorities outlined in the plan. The new artery carries particular significance for China's southwest, which has long lagged behind the more prosperous eastern coast and faced higher costs getting goods to seaports. Coal, ore, grain, new-energy materials and auto parts from the region can now take a more direct route to overseas markets. In the near term, the canal is likely to reshape existing cargo flows, with some freight shifting from road and rail to waterways and from the Pearl River Estuary to the Beibu Gulf, said Meng Shuang, an associate professor at Central University of Finance and Economics. Over time, Meng said, the lower cost of reaching the sea could generate new trade, draw investment inland and reshape industrial development along the canal. An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 4, 2026 shows a view of the China-Malaysia Qinzhou Industrial Park in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Cao Yiming) With China and ASEAN seeking closer economic ties and greater regional connectivity, experts say the Pinglu Canal could provide a new corridor for goods to flow in both directions between the vast Chinese and ASEAN markets. China's trade with ASEAN exceeded 1 trillion U.S. dollars for the first time last year. In the first seven months of 2026, total trade between the two sides reached 744.41 billion U.S. dollars, an increase of 24.7 percent year on year, accounting for 21.8 percent of China's total foreign trade during this period. BeBe Zhao, president of Singapore-China Integrated Developments (Guangxi) Pte. Ltd., said the canal could bring new opportunities for businesses on both sides. ASEAN products could move more efficiently into western China, while goods manufactured there could reach global markets through regional hubs such as Singapore. "The new route will not only make trade more efficient but also strengthen Singapore's role as a regional transshipment and trade hub," Zhao said. For Boonsub Panichakarn from the Faculty of Logistics and Digital Supply Chain at Naresuan University in Thailand, the canal's significance goes beyond the distance it saves. It lies in how much the canal can reduce logistics costs, time variability and uncertainty across the entire ASEAN-southwest China supply chain, he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing BEIJING, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged sustained efforts to expand and strengthen advanced manufacturing to provide strong support for advancing Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction, which was conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday. Efforts should be made to ensure both high-quality development and greater security, pursue smart, green and integrated development, and make the country's industrial chains more self-supporting and risk-resilient, Xi stressed. He emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and reinforce the foundations of the real economy. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a speech at the conference. Xi's important instructions provide essential guidance for developing advanced manufacturing, Li said, noting that China must treat developing advanced manufacturing as a major strategic task, and press steadily to boost its strength in manufacturing. Li stressed that next-generation intelligent manufacturing should serve as the primary direction, with greater emphasis on digital and intelligent empowerment, high-end manufacturing and self-reliance, green and low-carbon development, and cross-sector integration. Efforts should be made to continuously strengthen the innovation capacity, competitiveness and overall strength of advanced manufacturing, Li said. Li called for deepening the "AI plus manufacturing" initiative, stepping up guidance and support for enterprises' digital and intelligent transformation, and consolidating the foundation of intelligent software and hardware. China should also advance the deep integration of advanced manufacturing and modern services, foster service-oriented manufacturing, and cultivate advanced manufacturing clusters according to local conditions. In his concluding speech, Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, said China should further implement the initiative for high-quality development of key industrial chains, accelerate the building of a high-quality standards system, continue to address disorderly and irrational competition, and create a sound ecosystem for advanced manufacturing.
